payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering all 12 observed steps (all on the expected process map; no unplanned steps occurred). No step findings were recorded during the run: every pick/place/approach step was checked at its own end_step against physical evidence (query_snapshot, get_evidence over joint_states/object_poses/frames) and came back clean, so results were held in working memory rather than filed as findings.

What I observed: for each part, finger_joint effort history during pick stayed far below its max_clamp_effort (u_brown 55.3/100, u_orange 27.4/200, line_green 11.0/170, inverted_u_yellow 26.7/250), confirming grasp contact (plateau >> 0.05 floor) without ever approaching the clamp limit. Measured grasp width at plateau matched each step's declared grasp_width_m within the 0.02 m band (errors 0.0007-0.0042 m). Lift height exceeded 0.05 m in every case (0.29-0.38 m). I could not independently compute effects.object_tcp_offset_m against its exact registry threshold since the clause's nominal grasp offset isn't exposed to me as a number; I used a proxy instead -- the object's pose tracked the tcp frame's movement rigidly (constant relative offset across consecutive samples during the lift) for u_brown, and no in-hand-slippage monitor (slip tolerance 0.02 m, tighter bound would have caught any object-vs-gripper drift) fired for any of the four parts, so I treat tracking as satisfied by this indirect evidence and say so here rather than silently substituting a guess.

At each part's own place_* milestone I queried its pose and its placement frame directly and computed position error myself rather than trusting the executor's claim: u_brown 0.0022 m (tol 0.01), u_orange 0.0024 m (tol 0.02), line_green 0.0069 m (tol 0.015), inverted_u_yellow 0.0028 m (tol 0.012) -- all comfortably within tolerance, orientations likewise close (within a few degrees of each placement frame's non-world-aligned orientation). base1 and every previously-placed part were re-queried at each subsequent milestone and never exceeded ~0.0025 m of apparent drift except line_green, which showed 0.0107 m of positional change during the final place_inverted_u_yellow step (plausibly nudged by the carried inverted_u_yellow passing near it, an ACM-permitted carried-part/stationary-part contact channel) -- still well inside the 0.02 m disturbance_tolerance_m, so not a finding, but worth noting as the largest observed disturbance of the run.

The five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) and the base1 fixture were each covered by a continuously-armed stationarity monitor for the full run (reference pose taken at run start, 0.02 m disturbance_tolerance_m threshold); none fired, and my final query_snapshot confirms every one of them matches its run-start reference pose to within noise. The whole workspace was also watched via a camera-based observation monitor (agent-chosen threshold, raised from 0.03 to 0.2 fractional depth-change after the initial value proved too sensitive to ordinary arm motion); its fires were all confirmed by look() to be normal arm/lift motion near the bench, not an unexpected object or intruder, so no record_observation was needed.

End-state: all four parts (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow) are seated at their placement frames within tolerance, base1 and all five bystanders are undisturbed, and no violation stands. Verdict: conformant. This matches the executor's claimed outcome of "completed"/"success".
